TABLE_MODE.Controls.Title: Table Mode
TABLE_MODE.Controls.ToggleViewbox: Toggle Viewbox (drag to move, bottom-right handle to resize)
TABLE_MODE.Settings.VttUser.Name: VTT User
TABLE_MODE.Settings.VttUser.Hint: The Foundry user whose client renders on the table TV. Viewport commands are sent to this user. GM accounts are excluded; Assistant GM is allowed.
TABLE_MODE.Settings.VttAspect.Name: VTT Screen Aspect Ratio
TABLE_MODE.Settings.VttAspect.Hint: Locks the viewbox to this aspect ratio. Use 'Auto' to detect the VTT client's actual screen. Override if auto-detection gives wrong results.
TABLE_MODE.Settings.AnimationDuration.Hi: Duration of the pan/zoom animation when the VTT client receives a viewport sync.
TABLE_MODE.Settings.HideUi.Name: Hide VTT UI (minimal canvas view)
TABLE_MODE.Settings.HideUi.Hint: Hides all UI chrome on the VTT client — sidebar, chat, scene navigation, player list, hotbar, scene controls, logo, pause indicator. Applies to the VTT client only. GM UI is not affected.
TABLE_MODE.Settings.HideGmCursor.Name: Hide GM cursor on VTT
TABLE_MODE.Settings.HideGmCursor.Hint: Suppresses the GM's cursor and ruler on the VTT client. Players don't see the GM's mouse moving across the table TV. Pings remain visible (so the GM can still draw attention to specific spots). Applies to the VTT client only.
Default new tokens hidden on VTT + actor-name nameplate

When enabled, every newly-placed token: (1) is hidden ONLY on the VTT client (the table TV) — visible to GM and other players, and vision/fog still works normally for the VTT user, (2) has its nameplate set to 'Owner' (visible to GM, hidden from players), (3) takes its name from the linked Actor (instead of the prototype-token's possibly-generic default). Useful for the physical-minis workflow — players use real miniatures on the table TV, the digital token stays invisible on the TV until you toggle it via the eye in the Token HUD or the bulk toolbar button. Applies on token creation only; existing tokens are unaffected. NOTE: this does NOT set Foundry's native 'hidden' flag — that would block vision sharing.
